To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the removal of vitamin and mineral premixes from the diet for the final 28 d of the finishing phase of growth decreased bone mineral density and strength and increased bone resorption and formation in pigs.
supplement withdrawal increased serum osteocalcin concentrations and decreased bone quality in pigs.

supplement withdrawal (removing inorganic P, vitamins, and trace minerals from the diet) increases bone turnover (osteocalcin and pyrindinoline) and decreases bone strength (peak load, ultimate shear force, and ash content), but does not affect the incidence of bone fracture at slaughter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of supplement withdrawal and dietary wheat middling inclusion in the diet on the incidence of bone fracture, bone quality and bone metabolism in pigs.
determining the impact that supplement withdrawal and wheat inclusion has on bone metabolism and bone quality in pigs.
the impact of dietary factors on bone quality and the incidence of leg weakness and bone fractures in pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the removal of inorganic P, vitamins, and trace mineral supplements 28 d preslaughters decreases bone quality, increases bone turnover, and has no effect on the incidence of bone fracture at slaughter in pigs.
supplement withdrawal increases bone turnover, decreases bone strength, and does not alter bone fracture incidence at slaughter.
supplement withdrawal for 28 d prior to slaughter increased bone turnover and decreased bone strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

bone quality in the third metacarpal bone was not altered by dietary inclusion of 5,15, or 25% wheat middlings, and that supplement withdrawal increased the incidence of bone turnover and reduced bone quality in the preslaughter pig, but did not affect the incidence of bone fracture at slaughter.
supplement withdrawal increases bone turnover and bone fracture incidence in growing pigs.
the inclusion of 30% wheat middlings in the diet of weanling pigs did not adversely impact bone strength and bone density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supplement withdrawal for 28 d before slaughter decreases bone quality.
the inclusion of wheat middlings in nursery diets did not alter bone metabolism or bone quality.
